title: Use of table values and scientific calculator to find squares
competency: Find the square of a decimal using a table of squares and a calculator.

keywords.def: Writing a number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.
A table at the end of the book that gives x² for x from 1.00 to 9.99.

en.text: In scientific notation a number is written as a × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ a < 10. 450 = 4.5 × 10² and 0.0045 = 4.5 × 10⁻³. It helps when you use the table of squares.

am.text: በሳይንሳዊ አጻጻፍ ቁጥር a × 10ⁿ ሆኖ ይጻፋል፤ 1 ≤ a < 10። 450 = 4.5 × 10²።

screens.title: Activity 2.2
screens.ask: How can you write 450 using a number between 1 and 10?
screens.after: 450 = 4.5 × 100 = 4.5 × 10². This way of writing is called scientific notation. (45 × 10 is also 450, but 45 is not between 1 and 10.)

screens.title: Scientific notation
paras: A number is in scientific notation when it is written as a × 10ⁿ.
Here 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.
Big number: move the point left, n is positive. 450 = 4.5 × 10².
Small number: move the point right, n is negative. 0.0045 = 4.5 × 10⁻³.
screens.note: Count how many places the point moves. That count is n.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Writing a number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.

screens.text: Write the small number 0.0045 in scientific notation (a number from 1 to 10, times a power of 10).
screens.why:
Step 1: move the point right until you get a number from 1 to 10: 0.0045 → 4.5.
Step 2: count the moves: 3 places.
Step 3: moving right means the number was small, so the power is negative: 10⁻³.
So 0.0045 = 4.5 × 10⁻³. (45 × 10⁻⁴ has the right value, but 45 is not between 1 and 10.)
screens.clue: How many places must the point move to get a number between 1 and 10?

screens.ask: Scientific notation: write 84.3 as a number from 1 to 10 times 10. 84.3 = ___ × 10¹
screens.why:
Step 1: we need a number from 1 to 10, so move the point 1 place left: 84.3 → 8.43.
Step 2: 1 move left means × 10¹.
Check: 8.43 × 10 = 84.3.
So 84.3 = 8.43 × 10¹.
screens.clue: The first number must be between 1 and 10.

screens.text: Scientific notation for a number less than 1: 0.256 = ?
screens.why:
0.256 is less than 1, so the power of 10 is negative.
Move the point 1 place right: 0.256 → 2.56.
1 move right → 10⁻¹.
So 0.256 = 2.56 × 10⁻¹. (25.6 and 256 are not between 1 and 10.)
screens.clue: Is the number bigger or smaller than 1?

screens.text: Spot the mistake: which one is NOT written in scientific notation?
screens.why:
Scientific notation needs the first number from 1 up to (not including) 10.
12.5 is bigger than 10, so 12.5 × 10³ is not in scientific notation.
Correct form: 12.5 × 10³ = 1.25 × 10⁴.
screens.clue: Check the first number: is it at least 1 and less than 10?

en.text: The table of squares gives x² for x from 1.0 to 9.9 with a third digit across the top. Find the row with the first two digits, move right to the column of the third digit, and read the value. A table value is rounded; a calculator gives the exact value.

am.text: የካሬዎች ሰንጠረዥ ከ 1.0 እስከ 9.9 ላሉ ቁጥሮች ካሬውን ይሰጣል። የመጀመሪያዎቹን ሁለት አሃዞች ረድፍ፣ ሦስተኛውን አሃዝ አምድ ፈልግ።

screens.title: A faster way
screens.ask: Multiplying 3.24 × 3.24 by hand is slow. What would help most?
screens.after: The book has a table of squares at the end. It gives the square quickly and closely.

screens.title: The table of squares
paras: Squaring decimals by hand is slow.
A table of squares is printed at the end of the book.
The first column, x, lists 1.0 to 9.9. The top row gives the third digit, 0 to 9.

screens.title: Example 2.7: find (3.24)² in the table
screens.intro: Watch how to read the table. Tap ▶ for each step.

screens.title: Your turn: tap any number
screens.intro: Tap a number. The table shows which row and column it comes from.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A table at the end of the book that gives x² for x from 1.00 to 9.99.

screens.title: (6.75)² three ways
steps: The table is close to exact. The rough method is only a quick check.

screens.why:
3.27 → the first two digits are 3.2, so use row 3.2.
The third digit is 7, so use column 7.
Row 3.2 and column 7 meet at 10.69.
Check: 3.27 × 3.27 = 10.6929 ≈ 10.69.
screens.clue: Open the table: row 3.2, then column 7.

screens.title: Find (3.29)² in the table
screens.why:
3.29 → row 3.2 (first two digits).
Third digit 9 → column 9.
They meet at 10.82, so (3.29)² ≈ 10.82.
screens.clue: First find row 3.2. Then move right to column 9.

screens.why:
3.22 → row 3.2, column 2.
The table gives 10.37.
Exactly, 3.22 × 3.22 = 10.3684.
So 10.30 is wrong. False.

screens.text: Which row and column of the table give (5.29)²?
screens.why:
The row is the first two digits: 5.2.
The column is the third digit: 9.
So use row 5.2, column 9.

screens.ask: Use a calculator, or multiply by hand: (8.95)² = ___
screens.why:
8.95 × 8.95: without the points, 895 × 895 = 801 025.
8.95 has 2 decimal places, so the product has 2 + 2 = 4.
So (8.95)² = 80.1025 (exact).

screens.text: Rough, table and calculator give (8.95)² ≈ 81, ≈ 80.10 and = 80.1025. Which statement is true?
opts: The calculator is exact; the table is rounded; the rough value is a quick check
The rough value is the most accurate
screens.ans: The calculator is exact; the table is rounded; the rough value is a quick check
screens.why:
Rough: 8.95 ≈ 9, and 9² = 81. Fast, but only close.
Table: 80.10, rounded to 4 figures. Very close.
Calculator: 80.1025, every digit. Exact.
screens.clue: Which method uses all the digits?

en.text: If you move the decimal point of x one place, the decimal point of x² moves two places the same way. (36.7)² = (3.67)² × 100 and (0.367)² = (3.67)² × 0.01.

am.text: የ x ነጥብ አንድ ቦታ ሲንቀሳቀስ የ x² ነጥብ ሁለት ቦታ ይንቀሳቀሳል። (36.7)² = (3.67)² × 100።

screens.title: Ten times bigger
screens.after: 30² = 30 × 30 = 900. Ten times the number gives a hundred times the square.

screens.title: Numbers outside 1 to 10
paras: For other numbers, use scientific notation.
table: 1 place in x → 2 places in x²
2 places in x → 4 places in x²

screens.title: Key word again
defs: Writing a number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.

screens.title: If (3.67)² = 13.47, find (36.7)²
steps: So (36.7)² ≈ 1347. The point moved 1 place in x and 2 places in x².

screens.why:
Step 1: write 0.367 in scientific notation: 3.67 × 10⁻¹.
Step 2: square both parts: (3.67)² × (10⁻¹)² = 13.47 × 10⁻².
Step 3: × 10⁻² means move the point 2 places left: 0.1347.
screens.clue: The point moves 1 place left in x, so 2 places left in x².

screens.why:
367 = 3.67 × 10² (point moved 2 places).
Square: 13.47 × (10²)² = 13.47 × 10⁴.
× 10⁴ moves the point 4 places right: 134 700.
Exactly, 367² = 134 689; 13.47 was rounded.

screens.text: Moving the point with a letter: if (8.435)² = x, then (84.35)² = ?
screens.clue: Moving the point 1 place multiplies the square by 10².

screens.text: Moving the point with a letter: if (8.435)² = x, then (0.8435)² = ?
screens.why:
0.8435 = 8.435 × 10⁻¹.
Square: x × (10⁻¹)² = x × 10⁻² = x/100.
The number got smaller, so the square gets smaller too.
screens.clue: The point moves left, so the square gets smaller.

screens.why:
0.0743 = 7.43 × 10⁻² (the point moved 2 places left).
Square: 55.20 × (10⁻²)² = 55.20 × 10⁻⁴.
× 10⁻⁴ moves the point 4 places left: 0.005520.
screens.clue: The point moved 2 places, so it moves 4 places in the square.

items.text: Check with a rough estimate. True or false? (3.56)² = 30.91
items.why:
Rough check: 3.56 ≈ 4 and 4² = 16. 30.91 is far too big.
Table: row 3.5, column 6 gives 12.67.
So the statement is false.

9.9 and 9.801 are different numbers.
Different numbers have different squares: (9.9)² = 98.01, (9.801)² ≈ 96.06.
False.
items.clue: Are the two numbers being squared the same?

items.why:
8.95 → the digit 9 is 5 or more → round up to 9.
9² = 81.

notes.text: The book's full table of squares is on pp. 243–245. The app draws the rows it needs (computed exactly, rounded to 4 figures like the book).
Exercise 2.3 Q1 b "(3.56)² = 30.91": 30.91 is the table value of (5.56)²; probably a typo for 5.56. Q1 c "(9.9)² = (9.801)²" was probably meant as (9.9)² = 98.01. Both are kept false as printed.
